title: Registry enum, format v2
description: One controlled vocabulary in enums/v2, plus the rules that convert v1 values into it. See enums/v2/README.md for how conversions are evaluated. Rules a JSON Schema cannot express (definitions cover every value, every v1 value converts exactly once, targets exist) are checked by ci/enum_v2.py.

name.description: Registry name. The file is enums/v2/<name with _ replaced by ->.json.

description.description: The one question this vocabulary answers.

values.description: Allowed values, in presentation order. A plain string list, as in enums/v1, so existing generators can read it.

definitions.description: What each value means. Keys must equal `values` exactly.

standard.description: The standard this vocabulary follows, or an explicit statement that none applies.

relationship.description: `exact`: the values are the standard's terms. `adapted`: follows the standard with stated differences.

note.description: Required in practice for `adapted`: what differs and why.

since.description: traust-contracts version this file first shipped in.

replaces_v1.description: v1 registry enums whose values this file converts. Each v1 enum is owned by exactly one v2 file; empty for vocabularies with no v1 predecessor.

aliases_from_v1.description: Conversion rules, one or more per v1 value of every enum in `replaces_v1`. Order matters: for a given v1 value, conditional rules are tried in file order before its single unconditional rule.

when.description: All conditions must hold. Fields are named relative to the object that holds the v1 value.

to.description: Everything the v1 value becomes. Several effects express a value that splits across vocabularies.

equals.description: The field equals this JSON value.

in.description: The field equals one of these JSON values.

matches.description: The field is a string matching this regular expression (search, not full match).

contains_any.description: The field is an array holding at least one of these values.

enum.description: v2 registry name; the value lands in whichever field the v2 schema stores that vocabulary in.

value.description: Literal JSON value for a field that is not a vocabulary (e.g. is_default: true).

drop.description: The v1 value has no v2 counterpart; say where its information lives instead.
